hypotheses.text: Cycle 1 (B66 independent review, M1; owner decision 2026-11-03: allow one new paid call): a relisted posting with unchanged text meets its own settled operation under the same idempotency key once retention has deleted its record, so it is blocked for good. Hypothesis: a per-posting cleared_count (migration 0026), incremented by retention and appended to the extraction key only when above zero, makes a relisted posting extract again with exactly one new paid call, leaves every existing key and record unchanged (never-cleared postings), and keeps repeats free. Testable: an integration test that extracts, clears, relists the same text and extracts again sees two settled operations and a stored record, and a third attempt makes no call; it fails before the change.

Cycle 2 (B66 re-review, M1 and L1): an extraction pass works from rows read at its start, so a posting retention clears mid-pass reaches the service as live, meets a deleted record and an incremented count, and pays a new key with expired text, spending the key its relisting needs; and after a ledger refusal the pass recomputes the key, which retention may have changed. Hypothesis: reading tombstoned_at and cleared_count together from the stored row right before any money moves (a cleared posting returns 'tombstoned', sends and pays nothing) and carrying the key actually used on the refusal makes a count above zero on a live row mean a relisting only, and the refusal lookup always find the call's own operation. Testable: a pass whose first call clears a second posting counts it tombstoned_skipped with no operation; a refusal carries the key the call used; a real import revival keeps cleared_count; all fail before the change.
